content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data).**

What I found:
- **§13 (p0088)** vests ownership of all IP in the "Work" in Garman, expressly including "Improvements or Modifications thereto", and confirms no title passes to us. "Modifications" is defined (§1(n)/p0014) as the modifications in Schedule "D" — the bespoke work we commission and pay for.
- The only licence back is **§2 (p0028)**: a non-transferable, non-exclusive licence to use the *Software* and *Documentation* at Authorized Locations — it does not on its face reach Improvements/Modifications, and §3(c)–(d) bar sublicensing and reverse engineering. §17(a) does at least make the licence perpetual while fees are paid, which mitigates part of the gap.
- **No Customer Data ownership statement anywhere.** §4(b) has Garman converting "Sparkling's data" and §14 treats it only as mutual Confidential Information — confidentiality is not a rights-retention statement.

Why deviation rather than compliant: Garman retaining its platform IP is acceptable, but vendor ownership of customer-funded deliverables without a clear perpetual, modify/sublicence-capable licence back, combined with silence on our data, fails both the preferred and the fallback position on material terms.

Redline (validated, `ok:true`): a single inserted sentence pair after §13 confirming (i) we retain all right, title and interest in our data and pre-existing IP, with no assignment to Garman, and (ii) the §2 licence extends to Improvements and Modifications on a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free basis subject to §17(a). Garman's ownership of its underlying software is left untouched.
